items.label: section_header
items.text: LEARNINGOBJECTIVES

items.label: list_item
items.text: Understand that the total entropy change of any reaction is the sum of the entropy change of the system and the entropy change of the surroundings,summarised by the expression:

items.label: text
items.text: Stotal =Ssystem +Ssurroundings

items.label: list_item
items.text: Be able to calculate the entropy change of the system for a reaction, Ssystem given the entropies of the reactants and products.

items.label: list_item
items.text: Be able to calculate the entropy change of the surroundings, and hence Stotal, using the expression

items.label: list_item
items.text: Understand that the feasibility of a reaction depends on:

items.label: list_item
items.text: (i) the balance between Ssystem and Ssuroundings so that even endothermic reactions can occur spontaneously at room temperature

items.label: list_item
items.text: (i) temperature, as higher temperatures decrease the magnitude ofSsuroundings so its contribution to Stota is less.

items.label: list_item
items.text: Understand that reactions can occur as long as Stota is positive even if one of the other entropy changes is negative.

items.label: list_item
items.text: Understand and distinguishbetween theconcepts of thermodynamicstability andkineticstability.

items.label: section_header
items.text: TOTAL ENTROPY CHANGE, △Stotal

items.label: text
items.text: The total entropy change of a processcomprises two components:

items.label: list_item
items.text: ·the entropy change of the system, Ssystem, and

items.label: list_item
items.text: · the entropy change of the surroundings, Ssuroundings-

items.label: text
items.text: In a chemical reaction, the system is the species that are taking part in the reaction.

items.label: text
items.text: The surroundings is everything else. In practice, this usually means the reaction vessel, e.g. test tube or beaker, and the air in the laboratory.

items.label: text
items.text: changeof thesurroundings.Thatis:

items.label: formula
items.text: ΔS_total = ΔS_system + ΔS_surroundings

items.label: text
items.text: For a reaction to be spontaneous,△Stotal must be positive. This is another way of expressing the Second Lawof Thermodynamics.
